sentences.zh: 他们当时觉得，我怎么完成这项作业？

sentences.en: of a McDonald's to be able to do my learning.

sentences.en: Babies were actually doing that?
sentences.zh: 真的是小孩子在那样做吗？

sentences.en: Yes, students were doing that.
sentences.zh: 是的，学生们就是这么做的。

sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，没有网络接入的人因为无法进行视频预约，

sentences.zh: 而且缺乏网络接入

sentences.en: isn't just in rural areas as is often assumed.
sentences.zh: 并不像通常认为的那样只存在于农村地区。

sentences.en: have any internet access at all, not even through the data plan on their cell phones.
sentences.zh: 完全没有任何网络接入，甚至连手机数据套餐都没有。

sentences.en: decades into the 21st century.

sentences.zh: 然而说到线上生活，美国很大一部分地区

sentences.zh: 因此，为了解我们是怎么走到这一步的以及我们能做些什么，我们将

sentences.en: talking to a reporter and longtime friend of the show, Katie Thornton, who's been looking into this for
sentences.zh: 采访一位记者兼本节目的老朋友凯蒂·桑顿，她一直在为我们

sentences.en: us.
sentences.zh: 深入调查此事。

sentences.en: Hey, Katie.
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯蒂。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So, Katie, it's 2022.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯蒂，现在是2022年。

sentences.en: Why don't we have internet?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们还没有网络？

sentences.en: Well, it's actually because AOL didn't deliver enough of those CD-ROMs back in like 1995.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实是因为美国在线（AOL）在1995年左右没有派发足够多的光盘。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, that's definitely an old reference.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是个老梗了。

sentences.en: Are you?
sentences.zh: 你是……

sentences.en: I feel like you're too young to remember
sentences.zh: 我觉得你太年轻了，应该不记得

sentences.en: those.
sentences.zh: 那些东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, I have like the faintest memories of like teething on an AOL CD.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我对啃AOL光盘长牙这件事只有极其微弱的记忆。

sentences.en: But Roman, to actually answer your question about why there's this lack of access today in 2022,
sentences.zh: 但罗曼，要真正回答你关于为什么2022年今天还缺乏网络连接的问题，

sentences.en: first, we need a quick primer on how the internet actually works, like what the internet physically
sentences.zh: 首先我们需要做一个简短的科普，了解互联网到底是如何运作的，也就是互联网的物理形态

sentences.en: is, because it turns out Senator Ted Stevens of Alaska was kind of right.
sentences.zh: 是什么样的，因为事实证明，阿拉斯加参议员泰德·史蒂文斯某种程度上是对的。

sentences.en: The internet is not something that you just dump something on.
sentences.zh: 互联网不是你可以随便往上面倾倒东西的物件。

sentences.en: It's not a big truck.
sentences.zh: 它不是一辆大卡车。

sentences.en: It's a series
sentences.zh: 它是一系列

sentences.en: of tubes.
sentences.zh: 管道。

sentences.en: Just so people understand, like, in a sense, the internet really is tubes.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家明白，从某种意义上说，互联网真的就是管道。

sentences.en: It's these fiber optic
sentences.zh: 它们是铺设在街道下方、铁轨沿线，

sentences.en: cables that run under streets, along train tracks, and connect with these very large, energy-sucking,
sentences.zh: 并连接着那些超大型、极度耗电的庞大服务器农场的

sentences.en: enormous server farMs.
sentences.zh: 光纤电缆。

sentences.en: This is Greta Byram.
sentences.zh: 这位是格雷塔·拜勒姆。

sentences.en: She's been working on community internet projects for over 10 years.
sentences.zh: 她从事社区互联网项目已经超过10年了。

sentences.en: And perhaps fittingly for this story, we spoke over a really crappy internet connection.
sentences.zh: 而且对于这个故事来说，非常应景的是，我们是通过一段巨烂的网络连接进行采访的。

sentences.en: Your tubes were clogged.
sentences.zh: 你的管道堵塞了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But I think that this sort of tubiness is something that most people at this
sentences.zh: 但我想这种“管道化”的概念，大多数人

sentences.en: point do understand on a basic level.
sentences.zh: 到了现在在基础层面上都是理解的。

sentences.en: Like when you scroll Instagram, you're basically sending a
sentences.zh: 就像当你刷Instagram时，你基本上是在向远处的服务器农场发送

sentences.en: request to a distant server farm to find a certain piece of data and to send it back to your device.
sentences.zh: 请求，以寻找特定数据并将其发送回你的设备。

sentences.en: The only wireless part of that transaction is from your device to the Wi-Fi router.
sentences.zh: 整个交易中唯一的无线部分是从你的设备到Wi-Fi路由器。

sentences.en: But Greta says it's not the case that there is simply a single unobstructed connection going
sentences.zh: 但格雷塔说，并不是说服务器农场和家里的调制解调器之间

sentences.en: between a server farm and the modem in your home.
sentences.zh: 单纯存在一条畅通无阻的连接。

sentences.en: Instead, the data actually goes through roughly
sentences.zh: 相反，数据实际上要经过大约

sentences.en: three different layers of internet tubing, or what are sometimes called tiers.
sentences.zh: 三层不同的互联网管道，或者有时被称为层级结构。

sentences.en: And tier one is like these big backbone lines that span the country or go under oceans, like
sentences.zh: 第一层就像是跨越全国或穿过海底的大型骨干网线路，就像

sentences.en: these large companies that like you've never heard of.
sentences.zh: 那些你从未听说过的大公司。

sentences.en: So these are companies like Lumen Technologies, GTT, the Zayo Group.
sentences.zh: 所以这些公司包括 Lumen Technologies、GTT、扎尤集团（Zayo Group）。

sentences.en: Greta is correct.
sentences.zh: 格雷塔说得对。

sentences.en: I have never heard of these.
sentences.zh: 我确实没听说过这些公司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, neither had I.
sentences.zh: 不，我也没有。

sentences.en: But then there's also tier two, or what's called the middle mile,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外还有第二层，也就是所谓的中间英里（middle mile），

sentences.en: which often own like the cables connecting different cities within large regions.
sentences.zh: 它们通常拥有连接大区域内不同城市的电缆。

sentences.en: And layer two is sort of like transit, like kind of long stretches of towers.
sentences.zh: 第二层有点像运输网络，类似于长距离的信号塔。

sentences.en: And they also don't sell to like individuals or households.
sentences.zh: 而且它们也不向个人或住户销售服务。

sentences.en: So have I at least heard of these middle mile companies?
sentences.zh: 那我至少听说过这些中间英里公司吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道，罗曼。

sentences.en: Have you heard of Stealth Communications or Fiber Noir or my favorite, Internap?
sentences.zh: 你听说过 Stealth Communications、Fiber Noir，或者我最喜欢的 Internap 吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No, I think, yeah, heretofore I've been ignorant of Internet.
sentences.zh: 没有，我想，是的，在此之前我对互联网一无所知。

sentences.en: Well, it's okay that you were snoozing on Internet, because for our purposes,
sentences.zh: 好吧，你对互联网孤陋寡闻也没关系，因为对我们的目的而言，

sentences.en: you don't really need to know the names of these companies.
sentences.zh: 你其实不需要知道这些公司的名字。

sentences.en: All you need to know is that tier one and tier two connections, they're faSt.
sentences.zh: 你只需要知道第一层和第二层的连接速度非常快。

sentences.en: And that's because tier one and two companies only need to connect a few big facilities.
sentences.zh: 那是因为第一层和第二层的公司只需要连接少数几个大型设施。

sentences.en: So there's kind of like the interstate highway system or the, you know, airport hub and spoke system.
sentences.zh: 所以它有点像州际公路系统，或者说，你知道的，机场的枢纽辐射系统。

sentences.en: There's not too many of them, and they only go between a few key spots.
sentences.zh: 它们的数量不多，而且只在几个关键点之间运行。

sentences.en: Yeah, precisely.
sentences.zh: 对，确切地说。

sentences.en: So it's always been relatively affordable for them to lay down these high-capacity fiber lines.
sentences.zh: 因此，对它们来说，铺设这些高容量光纤线路一直以来都相对负担得起。

sentences.en: And fiber is like the really good stuff.
sentences.zh: 光纤可是真正的优质好东西。

sentences.en: It's basically bundles of flexible strands of glass, the width of human hair,
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一束束只有人类头发丝宽度的柔性玻璃纤维，

sentences.en: that can handle really large amounts of data.
sentences.zh: 能够处理极大量的海量数据。

sentences.en: It's by far the fastest and most reliable type of connection.
sentences.zh: 它是迄今为止速度最快、最稳定的连接类型。

sentences.en: But there's one final leap that the data has to make to get to us, Roman.
sentences.zh: 但数据要传送到我们这里，还要经历最后关键的一跃，罗曼。

sentences.en: And that's called tier three.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的第三层。

sentences.en: And tier three are your local retail Internet providers, your Spectrums and Verizons and such.
sentences.zh: 第三层就是你当地的零售互联网供应商，比如Spectrum、Verizon之类的主流公司。

sentences.en: Yes, finally, we're getting to names I know.
sentences.zh: 太好了，终于讲到我知道的名字了。

sentences.en: Well, good, because it's actually here at tier three that our broadband access problems truly begin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很好，因为实际上正是在这第三层，我们的宽带接入问题才真正开始。

sentences.en: Okay, so why is that?
sentences.zh: 好吧，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, it's because tier three companies like Verizon, they might own and operate their own tier one and tier two networks or purchase access from others.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是因为像Verizon这样的第三层公司，它们可能拥有并运营自己的第一层和第二层网络，或者从其他公司购买接入服务。

sentences.en: But either way, they're stuck with the task of figuring out what's called the last mile.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，它们都必须硬着头皮去解决所谓的“最后一公里”问题。

sentences.en: And the last mile is all the millions of tiny connections that go down various streets and under or over people's driveways, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 最后一公里就是通往各条街道、铺设在人们车道下方或上方的数百万个微小连接，等等等等。

sentences.en: And building the last mile, like building the tier three piece, it's very physical.
sentences.zh: 而建设最后一公里，就像建设第三层一样，是非常注重实体劳动的。

sentences.en: Like you're going up on the roofs and you're installing equipment and you're dealing with street furniture.
sentences.zh: 比如你要爬上屋顶安装设备，还要处理各种街道设施。

sentences.en: And like that part is just incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且这部分工作简直难得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Not to mention digging up roads and burying wires.
sentences.zh: 更不用说还要掘开道路、掩埋电缆了。

sentences.en: Totally, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意，完全同意。

sentences.en: And tier three companies are the ones left to do this for entire cities and sometimes entire regions.
sentences.zh: 而第三层公司就是那些得为整座城市甚至整个地区去干这块苦差事的企业。

sentences.en: So even though the last mile sounds way less sexy and high tech than country and ocean-spanning fiber backbones, it's way more expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管“最后一公里”听起来远不如横跨国家和海洋的光纤骨干网那么性感和高科技，但它的成本要高得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can totally see that.
sentences.zh: 是的，这完全可以想见。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So instead of fiber, most people's internet is traveling that last mile over wires that were first laid for totally different purposes.
sentences.zh: 因此，大多数人的互联网并没有使用光纤，而是在最后一公里通过最初为完全不同目的铺设的电缆传输。

sentences.en: Which is why a telephone company like AT&T might also be your internet provider.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么像AT&T这样的电话公司也可能成为你的互联网供应商。

sentences.en: Because you're using the copper lines originally provided for your telephone connection.
sentences.zh: 因为你在使用原本为你的电话连接提供的铜线。

sentences.en: Or the coaxial lines normally used for cable TV.
sentences.zh: 或者是通常用于有线电视的同轴电缆。

sentences.en: And internet signals can travel over both copper and coaxial, but they're slower than fiber and less reliable.
sentences.zh: 互联网信号可以通过铜线和同轴电缆传输，但它们比光纤速度慢，稳定性也较差。

sentences.en: Like this is when like your internet service provider says, oh, we have fast DSL.
sentences.zh: 就像当你的互联网服务商说，哦，我们有高速DSL时，

sentences.en: That just means like we're sending the signal over copper lines.
sentences.zh: 这其实只意味着我们在通过铜线发送信号。

sentences.en: And watch out because if it rains, your signal might get really fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 当心点，因为如果下雨，你的信号可能会变得非常模糊不清。

sentences.en: So while something like dial-up might be mostly a thing of the past, the truth is copper phone lines still connect a lot of people to the internet over DSL.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然拨号上网之类的技术可能已经基本成为过去式，但事实是，铜质电话线仍然通过DSL将许多人连接到互联网。

sentences.en: And even many people's coaxial cable connections aren't fast enough to meet the federal government's definition of broadband.
sentences.zh: 甚至许多人的同轴有线电视连接也达不到联邦政府对宽带的定义。

sentences.en: And what is that definition?
sentences.zh: 那个定义是什么？

sentences.en: Right now, it's 25 megabits per second download speed and three megabits upload.
sentences.zh: 目前，下载速度是每秒25兆比特，上传速度是3兆比特。

sentences.en: And to be clear, you're saying megabits here.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，你这里说的是兆比特（Megabits）。

sentences.en: That's only like one-eighth of a megabyte.
sentences.zh: 那只有大约八分之一兆字节（Megabyte）。

sentences.en: So the speeds that you mentioned, particularly the three megabit upload speed, that's really slow.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到的速度，尤其是3兆比特的上传速度，真的很慢。

sentences.en: Like I have a house full of kids and between all of us, that would not even come close to being acceptable.
sentences.zh: 就像我家里有一群孩子，我们所有人加起来，这根本连达标都算不上。

sentences.en: No, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不算。

sentences.en: And this is why getting fiber into neglected areas is so important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么将光纤引入被忽视的地区如此重要。

sentences.en: But Greta says who gets fiber is determined by the market.
sentences.zh: 但格雷塔说，谁能用上光纤是由市场决定的。

sentences.en: And the market is determined not by who wants fiber, but really just who can afford it.
sentences.zh: 而市场不是由谁想要光纤决定的，实际上是由谁买得起决定的。

sentences.en: So if you're really lucky, you live in a neighborhood where companies see, oh, there's plenty of people who can afford $80 a month internet.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你非常幸运，你住在这样一个社区：公司看到，哦，这里有很多人付得起每月80美元的网费。

sentences.en: So we'll put a fiber line under the streets.
sentences.zh: 于是我们就在街道下面铺设一条光纤线路。

sentences.en: But if you live in a neighborhood where they do their market analysis and it looks like folks can't afford that, you're going to still be on copper or coax.
sentences.zh: 但如果你住在这样一个社区：他们做了市场分析，发现居民们负担不起这个费用，那你就会继续使用铜线或同轴电缆。

sentences.en: And so even though there are plenty of homes and businesses with fiber connections, for a lot of the country, that last mile remains a deep, vexing problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管有大量的住宅和企业拥有光纤连接，但对美国的大片地区而言，最后一公里依然是一个深然而棘手的问题。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to take a look at two examples of cities that were decidedly not rich cities,
sentences.zh: 所以我想看一看两个城市的例子，它们绝对不是富裕城市，

sentences.en: where people in the last decade went about pursuing this last mile problem in two very different ways.
sentences.zh: 过去十年里，人们以两种截然不同的方式着手解决这个最后一公里问题。

sentences.en: Okay, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Which is the first city?
sentences.zh: 第一个城市是哪个？

sentences.en: Up first is Detroit, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 首先是密歇根州的底特律。

sentences.en: The statistics in Detroit at that time were abysmal.
sentences.zh: 当时底特律的各项统计数据简直糟透了。

sentences.en: That's Monique Tate.
sentences.zh: 那是莫妮克·泰特。

sentences.en: She's a digital justice advocate and former auto worker who lives in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 她是一名数字正义倡导者、前汽车工人，住在底特律。

sentences.en: And the statistics she's citing are from 2014.
sentences.zh: 她引用的统计数据来自2014年。

sentences.en: And she says at that time, Detroit was ranked as the country's worst connected city.
sentences.zh: 她说，当时底特律被评为全美互联网络最差的城市。

sentences.en: 60% of people did not have a connection that met the minimum definition of broadband.
sentences.zh: 60%的人没有达到宽带最低定义要求的网络连接。

sentences.en: The number is astounding.
sentences.zh: 这个数字令人震惊。

sentences.en: That paralleled itself with 40% of the people lacking internet connectivity at all.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，有40%的人完全没有互联网连接。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So 40% of people with no internet, not even on their phones.
sentences.zh: 也就是说40%的人根本没有网，甚至手机上也没有。

sentences.en: Yeah, not even on their phones.
sentences.zh: 对，甚至手机上也没有。

sentences.en: And you have to remember, at this time in 2014, everything is moving online.
sentences.zh: 你得记住，在2014年的这个时候，一切都在向线上转移。

sentences.en: So if you aren't online, you are out of luck.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不上网，你就彻底没辙了。

sentences.en: Education, economic development and opportunity, which I'm relating to jobs, you are stricken from that.
sentences.zh: 教育、经济发展以及与工作相关的机遇，你统统都与它们无缘了。

sentences.en: Because if you go somewhere and say, I'm interested in a job, can I just fill out a piece of paper?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你去某个地方说，我对这份工作感兴趣，我能填张纸质表格吗？

sentences.en: No one has that for you to do anymore.
sentences.zh: 已经没人让你这么做了。

sentences.en: They're going to say, if you can't submit your application, we can't even consider you.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，如果你无法提交网申，我们甚至都不会考虑你。

sentences.en: So Monique watched as job opportunities dried up for folks who couldn't easily apply online.
sentences.zh: 因此，莫妮克眼睁睁地看着那些无法轻松进行网申的人的工作机会逐渐枯竭。

sentences.en: Or as the people who did have smartphones tried to format resumes on them.
sentences.zh: 或者那些拥有智能手机的人试图在上面排版简历。

sentences.en: And folks were always trying to find places with decent Wi-Fi, particularly around Detroit's North End neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 人们总是试图寻找Wi-Fi信号不错的地方，尤其是在底特律的北端社区附近。

sentences.en: In the greater North End, there is, of course, McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 在大北端，当然有麦当劳。

sentences.en: And you could go someplace like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以去那种地方。

sentences.en: But there was no local library in the greater North End.
sentences.zh: 但大北端没有当地的图书馆。

sentences.en: We were not even able to really look to the public provision of a library system.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至无法指望公共图书馆系统的供应。

sentences.en: Now, in some of these cases, people weren't able to get online because there was not an affordable option.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，人们无法上网是因为没有负担得起的选择。

sentences.en: And at the time, there was also large sections of Detroit that literally had no internet connection.
sentences.zh: 而且当时底特律有很大一部分地区实际上根本没有互联网连接。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Like all the Tier 3 stuff we talked about, the wires, the tunnels, just did not exist in some neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 就像我们讨论过的所有三级网络设施、电线、隧道，在某些社区根本不存在。

sentences.en: So I can see why they may not have fiber as an option, for the reasons you laid out earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以我能理解为什么正如你之前分析的那样，他们可能无法将光纤作为选项。

sentences.en: But to have no real internet infrastructure at all, no copper, no coaxial, how does that happen?
sentences.zh: 但竟然完全没有真正的互联网基础设施，没有铜缆，没有同轴电缆，这怎么可能发生？

sentences.en: I mean, that can't be random.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不可能是随机的吧。

sentences.en: No, it's not random.
sentences.zh: 不，这不是随机的。

sentences.en: Greta says a number of years ago, a researcher named Bill Callahan started looking into these patterns, starting with the city of Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 格里塔说，多年前，一位名叫比尔·卡拉汉的研究人员开始调查这些规律，首先从克利夫兰市开始。

sentences.en: And he got a hold of AT&T's maps of where they were investing in fiber infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他拿到了AT&T关于光纤基础设施投资地点的地图。

sentences.en: And he lined it up with the old redlining maps from the 40s and found that it's the same,
sentences.zh: 他将其与40年代的旧时红线区地图进行了对比，发现它们一模一样，

sentences.en: like it's the same streets that are the dividing lines between where the investment's happening and where it's not.
sentences.zh: 就像是同一条街道构成了有投资和无投资的分界线。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have to say that this does not surprise me at all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我得说这完全不出我的意料。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, sadly, me neither.
sentences.zh: 对，你知道，遗憾的是，我也不觉得意外。

sentences.en: This is a practice known as digital redlining.
sentences.zh: 这种做法被称为数字红线歧视。

sentences.en: And AT&T has said, no, we don't redline.
sentences.zh: AT&T曾表示，不，我们没有搞红线歧视。

sentences.en: But people have found evidence of digital redlining in Dallas, Toledo, Dayton, Louisville, Milwaukee, and also Detroit.
sentences.zh: 但人们在达拉斯、托莱多、代顿、路易斯维尔、密尔沃基以及底特律都发现了数字红线歧视的证据。

sentences.en: And so what was once explicitly racist policy is now just racist economic policy where companies can say, well, we will not recover the money that we put into these neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 因此，曾经明目张胆的种族政策，现在变成了纯粹的种族经济政策，大公司可以宣称，嗯，我们无法收回投入到这些社区的资金。

sentences.en: So this is just an economic decision.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一项经济决策。

sentences.en: Race has nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 与种族毫无关系。

sentences.en: But the outcome is the same.
sentences.zh: 但结果是一样的。

sentences.en: But also, Roman, when Internet companies did offer service, they didn't always make their fastest speeds available to everyone.
sentences.zh: 而且，罗曼，当互联网公司确实提供服务时，他们并不总是向所有人提供最快的网速。

sentences.en: For example, back in the mid-2010s, when Monique was working with Detroit residents, one of the city's major carriers, Comcast Xfinity,
sentences.zh: 例如，在2010年代中期，当莫妮克与底特律居民合作时，该市的主要运营商之一康卡斯特Xfinity，

sentences.en: offered a $9.95 a month deal to some low-income residents.
sentences.zh: 向一些低收入居民推出了每月9.95美元的优惠套餐。

sentences.en: They bragged about the fact that they were providing this program that low-income people could obtain.
sentences.zh: 他们吹嘘自己正在提供这个低收入群体可以获得的惠民项目。

sentences.en: In that program, there was 10 megabits of download speed and 1 megabit of upload speed.
sentences.zh: 在该项目中，下载速度为10兆位，上传速度为1兆位。

sentences.en: Jesus, that is so slow.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这也太慢了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it is insultingly slow.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，慢得简直是对人的侮辱。

sentences.en: It's not even close to the minimum requirement to be considered broadband.
sentences.zh: 这甚至连被视为宽带的最低标准都算不上。

sentences.en: So you're already saying to this underserved and underrepresented group, we're going to provide a substandard product.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上是在对这个服务不足、代表性不够的群体说，我们要提供一个不合格的产品。

sentences.en: So given that this was the state of things in Detroit, in the intervening years, like since 2014, what have people been doing to get more access?
sentences.zh: 鉴于底特律当时的情况，在随后的几年里，比如自2014年以来，人们为了获得更多的网络接入都做了些什么？

sentences.en: Because I can't believe it has stayed exactly like this this whole time.
sentences.zh: 因为我简直不敢相信它一直保持原状到现在。

sentences.en: Yeah, so what I'm about to tell you is going to kind of sound like kindergarten logic.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要告诉你的内容听起来可能有点像幼儿园逻辑。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But one of the solutions that was hit upon in some of these neighborhoods, and that's still being used in some of them today, started with the idea of sharing.
sentences.zh: 但在其中一些社区想出的解决方案之一，并且至今仍在其中一些社区中使用，始于分享的理念。

sentences.en: It sounded like a good idea, and it sounded really simple.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是个好主意，而且听起来非常简单。

sentences.en: It didn't require anything that seemed too illegal.
sentences.zh: 它不需要任何看起来过于违法的东西。

sentences.en: So this is Patrick Crouch.
sentences.zh: 这位是帕特里克·克劳奇。

sentences.en: Patrick is an urban farmer who, back in 2010, lived in North Corktown, which was one of these historically redlined neighborhoods in Detroit with digital access issues.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克是一名城市农民，早在2010年，他住在底特律的北科克敦，这是底特律历史上被划为红线、存在数字接入问题的社区之一。

sentences.en: So we didn't really have any internet, and the house was such that it wasn't wired for telephone, and it wasn't wired for cable.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上没有任何互联网，房子也没有预设电话线，也没有预设电缆。

sentences.en: And I was taking an online class, and it was at night, so that was after the libraries had closed.
sentences.zh: 当时我在上一个网课，而且是晚上，所以那时候图书馆已经关门了。

sentences.en: So I was like literally having to ride my bike two and a half miles to a friend who had internet connection that was willing to let me sit and take this class.
sentences.zh: 所以我 literalmente（字面意思上）不得不骑自行车两英里半去一个有网络连接的朋友家，他愿意让我坐在那儿上这门课。

sentences.en: So, Roman, most of Patrick's neighbors also couldn't get good internet, either because Comcast didn't service their address, or they didn't offer an affordable option.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，帕特里克的绝大多数邻居也无法获得好的网络，要么是因为康卡斯特不覆盖他们的地址，要么是因为他们没有提供经济实惠的选择。

sentences.en: But down the block from Patrick was a software engineer named Ben Chodorov.
sentences.zh: 但在帕特里克家街往下走的地方，住着一位名叫本·乔多罗夫的软件工程师。

sentences.en: You know, he was a computer person.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是个搞电脑的人。

sentences.en: I don't know what he does.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是做什么的。

sentences.en: He's tried to tell me what he does, and I still don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 他试图向我解释他是做什么的，但我还是听不懂。

sentences.en: And you see, Ben had this very rare thing in the neighborhood, a cable internet connection.
sentences.zh: 你看，本在社区里拥有这个非常稀罕的东西——有线宽带连接。

sentences.en: And he was happy to share it with Patrick, but he couldn't just tell him his Wi-Fi password and call it a day.
sentences.zh: 他很乐意与帕特里克分享，但他不能只是把Wi-Fi密码告诉他就完事了。

sentences.en: They lived way too far apart for that.
sentences.zh: 他们住得太远了，根本行不通。

sentences.en: So instead, Ben suggested an alternative approach.
sentences.zh: 于是，本提出了另一种替代方案。

sentences.en: He started talking about this mesh network thing.
sentences.zh: 他开始谈论这个叫网状网络的东西。

sentences.en: For me, it was the obvious solution.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是显而易见的解决方案。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a super fragile solution, definitely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是一个极其脆弱的解决方案。

sentences.en: But it was just like, yeah, we had to solve a problem.
sentences.zh: 但感觉就是，没错，我们必须解决一个问题。

sentences.en: This is Ben.
sentences.zh: 这位是本。

sentences.en: And the mesh network thing he was proposing would go way beyond sharing one lonely Wi-Fi signal with just one other person.
sentences.zh: 他所提议的网状网络远远超出了仅仅与另一个人分享一个孤立的Wi-Fi信号的范畴。

sentences.en: Instead, it was a way to bring wireless internet to a whole bunch of people all at once.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是一种同时为一大群人提供无线互联网的方法。

sentences.en: He says he started thinking about it when he was going through some of his old gear.
sentences.zh: 他说，当他在整理一些旧装备时，开始萌生了这个想法。

sentences.en: I had a pile of old little wireless radios that were, like, given to somebody who gave them to somebody else who gave them to me.
sentences.zh: 我有一堆旧的小型无线收音机设备，就像是有人送给另一个人，然后另一个人又转送给了我。

sentences.en: And so I ended up with this, like, box of pretty crappy wireless routers.
sentences.zh: 所以我最后得到了一箱相当破烂的无线路由器。

sentences.en: So Ben began handing out some of these free wireless routers to those few neighbors who also had good internet access and then asked if they could share their connections, too.
sentences.zh: 于是本开始将这些免费的无线路由器分发给那些同样拥有良好网络连接的少数邻居，并询问他们是否也愿意分享自己的网络连接。

sentences.en: So he would just, like, knock on the door and hand them some weird old equipment and say, like, please attach us to your modem and give me your password?
sentences.zh: 所以他就会去敲门，递给他们一些奇怪的旧设备，然后说，能把我们连到你的调制解调器上并把密码告诉我吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's pretty much exactly how it happened.
sentences.zh: 对，事情基本上就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, like, I already talked to all my neighbors.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我已经和所有的邻居都谈过了。

sentences.en: That made it easier to set up because people already trusted me somewhat.
sentences.zh: 这让搭建变得更容易了，因为大家对我本来就有些信任。

sentences.en: So the way that this whole thing works was that the person with internet access would attach a so-called radio to their normal at-home router.
sentences.zh: 整个运作方式是这样的：拥有互联网连接的人会将一个所谓的无线电收发器连接到他们平常的家用路由器上。

sentences.en: And they'd put that up on their roof or on the side of their house.
sentences.zh: 他们会把它安装在屋顶上或房屋侧面。

sentences.en: And that radio would basically extend the Wi-Fi signal so folks down the block could pick it up, too.
sentences.zh: 那个无线电收发器基本上会扩大Wi-Fi信号，这样街区里的其他人也能接收到。

sentences.en: And throughout the neighborhood, there were also these little wireless nodes that extended the signals even further.
sentences.zh: 在整个社区里，还有这些小型无线节点，它们能将信号传得更远。

sentences.en: And then Ben and his neighbors would climb up on the roof of whoever's house they were connecting and put up equipment to receive that signal.
sentences.zh: 然后本和他的邻居们会爬上他们要连接的任一住户的屋顶，安装接收信号的设备。

sentences.en: Then, as a final step, they'd connect a wire from that receiver into a home Wi-Fi router and bang, they would be online.
sentences.zh: 最后一步，他们将一根电线从接收器连接到家里的Wi-Fi路由器上，砰，他们就能上网了。

sentences.en: So in this kind of giant daisy chain of gear, what were the locations in the neighborhood where they installed some of these connections and nodes?
sentences.zh: 那么在这个巨大的菊花链式设备网络中，他们在社区里什么地方安装了这些连接和节点呢？

sentences.en: Well, so as far as I can tell from talking with Ben, the answer appears to be pretty much anywhere they could.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我和本交谈所知，答案似乎是：只要能装的地方都装了。

sentences.en: So, like, there was this hostel that donated their connection.
sentences.zh: 比如，有一家青年旅舍捐赠了他们的网络连接。

sentences.en: The other node was in my upstairs neighbor's chicken coop.
sentences.zh: 另一个节点在我楼上邻居的鸡舍里。

sentences.en: I think that was it.
sentences.zh: 我想就这些吧。

sentences.en: Did you talk to them?
sentences.zh: 你跟他们聊过吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, wait.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，等等。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, there was another node in an old Airstream trailer that was like a food truck.
sentences.zh: 对，还有一个节点在一辆老式清风房车里，那辆车就像一辆餐车。

sentences.en: So between these few internet access points and those few nodes, those extenders,
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些少数互联网接入点和这几个节点、中继器之间，

sentences.en: they made this web of wireless networks connecting a bunch of neighbors' houses and an apartment building and that hostel.
sentences.zh: 他们构建了一个无线网络网，连接了许多邻居的房屋、一栋公寓楼和那家青年旅舍。

sentences.en: So did the neighborhood need a password or was it just kind of open to anyone?
sentences.zh: 那社区需要密码吗？还是说对任何人都是开放的？

sentences.en: No, you didn't really need a password.
sentences.zh: 不，你实际上不需要密码。

sentences.en: Like, people who had routers on the network could put a password on their connection if they wanted to.
sentences.zh: 比如，网络上的路由器拥有者如果愿意的话，可以在他们的连接上设置密码。

sentences.en: But a lot of people just intentionally left theirs open so that other people could pick it up.
sentences.zh: 但很多人只是刻意让他们的网络保持开放，以便其他人可以使用。

sentences.en: Yeah, people would park right next to our house all the time.
sentences.zh: 对，人们经常把车停在我们房子旁边。

sentences.en: And people would, yeah, just roll up and sit there for, you know, an hour or two and do their thing.
sentences.zh: 人们会把车开过来，然后坐在那儿待上一两个小时，做他们自己的事情。

sentences.en: So it sounds like it worked.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实管用。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, according to Patrick, it did.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，根据帕特里克的说法，确实管用。

sentences.en: So this is what people that don't know about computers call magic.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那些不懂电脑的人所说的魔法。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, I mean.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我的意思是。

sentences.en: It was essentially magic as far as I could tell.
sentences.zh: 就我所能理解的而言，这基本上就是魔法。

sentences.en: I get that this was definitely better than no internet at all.
sentences.zh: 我明白这绝对比完全没有网要好。

sentences.en: But was it fast enough to get the job done?
sentences.zh: 但它的网速足够处理正事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was curious about this.
sentences.zh: 对，我对这一点很好奇。

sentences.en: It's true that because it involves sharing a limited number of broadband connections,
sentences.zh: 确实，由于这涉及到共享数量有限的宽带连接，

sentences.en: Patrick said he would save heavy bandwidth things like downloading music for Saturday mornings.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克说他会把下载音乐之类占用大量带宽的事情留到周六早上再做。

sentences.en: And sometimes that Airstream food truck would be out serving food to people.
sentences.zh: 有时那辆房车餐车会出来为人门提供餐饮服务。

sentences.en: Right, like doing what it's supposed to do, like go feed people instead of being a node on a mesh network.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像它本该做的那样，去给人们提供食物，而不是当网状网络上的一个节点。

sentences.en: Right, exactly, like doing a launch service.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，就像提供外卖服务一样。

sentences.en: But all in all, Ben's mesh network did the job.
sentences.zh: 但总而言之，本的网状网络确实发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Patrick says he never even bothered trying to get on Comcast for himself while he was on mesh.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克说，在使用网状网络期间，他甚至懒得去费心为自己申请康卡斯特的服务。

sentences.en: I mean, what's interesting about this is that this mesh network as an alternate solution to the last mile problem, it is not top down.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其中有趣的地方在于，作为解决最后一公里问题的替代方案，这个网状网络并非自上而下的。

sentences.en: It's not being solved by Comcast or some other tier three provider.
sentences.zh: 它不是由康卡斯特或其他三级运营商解决的。

sentences.en: It is really bottom up.
sentences.zh: 它是真正自下而上的。

sentences.en: The neighborhood is doing it for themselves.
sentences.zh: 是社区在自力更生。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I want to be very clear about this.
sentences.zh: 但我想对此明确一点。

sentences.en: Ben and Patrick definitely weren't the only ones in Detroit using mesh to fix this last mile problem.
sentences.zh: 本和帕特里克绝对不是底特律唯一使用网状网络来解决这个最后一公里问题的人。

sentences.en: It turned out that a lot of folks found themselves converging on this solution, including Monique Tate and Greta Byram.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，很多人发现自己都在向这个解决方案靠拢，其中包括莫妮克·泰特和格里塔·拜拉姆。

sentences.en: And those are the people, the experts that we talked to earlier.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们前面采访过的那些人，那些专家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the early 2010s, Monique and Greta helped form a group promoting internet access in Detroit that would come to be known as the Equitable Internet Initiative.
sentences.zh: 在2010年代初期，莫妮克和格里塔协助成立了一个在底特律推广互联网接入的组织，后来被称为“公平互联网倡议”。

sentences.en: And EII basically approached this idea of a homespun mesh network and really kind of formalized it and scaled it up.
sentences.zh: EII基本上采用了这种民间自制的网状网络理念，并将其正式化、规模化。

sentences.en: They started a process of installing mesh in four different Detroit neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 他们开始在底特律四个不同的社区安装网状网络。

sentences.en: And then they trained residents on how to build and fix the networks and paid them for their work.
sentences.zh: 然后他们培训居民如何构建和修复网络，并为他们的工作支付报酬。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But eventually they got so big that they ran into a bit of a problem.
sentences.zh: 但最终他们的规模变得如此之大，以至于遇到了一些小麻烦。

sentences.en: As it became more popular, people did start to ask questions because comments were made that I think this might not be legal.
sentences.zh: 随着它变得越来越受欢迎，人们确实开始提出质疑，因为有人评论说，我觉得这可能不太合法。

sentences.en: Well, I was definitely beginning to wonder if it was legal.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我确实开始怀疑这是否合法了。

sentences.en: Well, technically, not exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，严格来说，并不完全是。

sentences.en: But this sort of realization actually turned out to be a really good thing in the end because it spurred them to do something extra cool,
sentences.zh: 但这种意识到最后其实是一件非常好的事，因为这促使他们做出了一些特别酷的举动，

sentences.en: which was to just go around Comcast entirely.
sentences.zh: 那就是彻底绕过康卡斯特。

sentences.en: Because in 2018, the Equitable Internet Initiative partnered with a Tier 2 provider.
sentences.zh: 因为在2018年，“公平互联网倡议”与一家二级服务提供商进行了合作。

sentences.en: And so that's the kind of company that buys internet access further up the chain, like closer to that big fiber internet backbone.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种在产业链上游购买互联网接入服务的公司，比如更接近那个大型光纤互联网骨干网的公司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that Tier 2 provider called 123Net now gives the Equitable Internet Initiative multiple free,
sentences.zh: 而那家名为123Net的二级服务提供商现在为“公平互联网倡议”提供多个免费的、

sentences.en: super fast fiber internet access points that EII then distributes wirelessly by mesh.
sentences.zh: 超高速光纤互联网接入点，然后由EII通过无线网状网络进行分发。

sentences.en: And that means the Equitable Internet Initiative no longer needs to purchase broadband from Comcast or any other Tier 3 provider.
sentences.zh: 这意味着“公平互联网倡议”不再需要从康卡斯特或任何其他三级提供商那里购买宽带了。

sentences.en: Because they are the Tier 3 provider.
sentences.zh: 因为他们自己就是三级提供商。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: They are Tier 3.
sentences.zh: 他们就是三级。

sentences.en: And this has increased the connection speeds of their users in some really meaningful ways.
sentences.zh: 这在一些非常关键的方面提升了他们用户的连接速度。

sentences.en: For example, their service now includes symmetrical download and upload speeds.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们的服务现在包括对称的下载和上传速度。

sentences.en: Because the key is to create not only just consumers, but create producers so that the upload of your content is just as important as the download of someone else's content.
sentences.zh: 因为关键不仅在于培养消费者，还要培养生产者，这样你上传内容的速度就和下载别人的内容速度一样重要。

sentences.en: So if you decided that you wanted to have a podcast, you could.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你决定想做一个播客，你完全可以。

sentences.en: And the neighborhood network that Monique was the manager of now delivers free broadband to about 135 households.
sentences.zh: 而莫妮卡曾担任管理者的社区网络现在为大约135户家庭提供免费宽带。

sentences.en: That's about 500 people.
sentences.zh: 大约有500人。

sentences.en: And that's just one of the three neighborhoods where the Equitable Internet Initiative has operational mesh networks.
sentences.zh: 这只是“公平互联网倡议”拥有运营中网状网络的三个社区之一。

sentences.en: Okay, so this brings me to my big question about mesh.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就引出了我对网状网络的一个重大疑问。

sentences.en: These numbers that you're saying, like 125 households in one neighborhood, there's three neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的这些数字，比如一个社区有125户，一共有三个社区。

sentences.en: That is super admirable and I'm so amazed and pleased.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常令人钦佩，我感到无比惊叹和高兴。

sentences.en: And it's a real success.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实是一个成功。

sentences.en: But those are small numbers compared to the size of the problem facing the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但与美国所面临的问题规模相比，这些数字实在是太小了。

sentences.en: overall.
sentences.zh: 总体而言。

sentences.en: And so my question, I guess, at the end of all this is, will this scale?
sentences.zh: 所以我想我最后的问题是，这能够规模化吗？

sentences.en: And do we even want, like, an ad hoc, you know, mesh network to be something that scales?
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至希望这种临时的、你知道的，网状网络成为一种能够规模化的东西吗？

sentences.en: Like, is this a workaround to a problem that should be solved, like, head on?
sentences.zh: 比如说，这算是一种对本来应该正面解决的问题的权宜之计吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that is definitely something that I wondered, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这也是我一直在纳闷的事情。

sentences.en: Because, like you say, it doesn't feel like the solution.
sentences.zh: 因为就像你说的，这感觉并不像是根本解决方案。

sentences.en: Some people are definitely trying to get mesh to scale.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实在努力让网状网络实现规模化。

sentences.en: But it turns out not everyone who has worked on mesh is convinced that it's a viable way forward, including, and I think this is pretty telling, Ben Chodorov,
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，并非所有研究过网状网络的人都相信这是一条可行的发展道路，其中包括——我认为这很能说明问题——本·乔多罗夫，

sentences.en: who set up that really early mesh network back around 2010.
sentences.zh: 他在2010年前后搭建了那个非常早期的网状网络。

sentences.en: I mean, I think I was naively hopeful in the early days, but that hopefulness definitely waned.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，早期时我曾天真地抱有希望，但这种希望确实逐渐减弱了。

sentences.en: The way Ben sees it, the network met an acute need for a while, and he is super proud of what he and his neighbors built together.
sentences.zh: 在本看来，这个网络在一段时间内满足了迫切的需求，他为自己和邻居们共同建设的成果感到无比自豪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But he thought of it as more of a conversation starter than anything.
sentences.zh: 但他认为这与其说是个解决方案，不如说是个引起对话的引子。

sentences.en: I saw that as, like, a political message that could be sent by our mesh networks, like, man, look what we had to do.
sentences.zh: 我当时把它看作是我们网状网络可以发出的一种政治讯息，比如，天哪，看看我们不得不做什么。

sentences.en: But then it's easy to massage that political message into saying, like, we don't have to change the big systems because we can just build our own.
sentences.zh: 但随后，人们很容易把这种政治诉求美化为：我们不需要改变庞大的系统，因为我们可以自己建一个。

sentences.en: And I think that's a way of ignoring the political organizing that has to happen to actually confront power and change it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种逃避政治组织工作的方式，而这些工作本来是真正去对抗权力和改变现状所必需的。

sentences.en: I mean, this reminds me of, like, those, like, heartwarming GoFundMe campaigns for someone to get a kidney transplant when, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让我想起了那些温馨的“浇筑基金”筹款活动，为了让某人能做肾脏移植，你知道的，

sentences.en: it's great that people are generous and somebody can get their kidney.
sentences.zh: 人们慷慨解囊、某人能换上肾脏当然很好。

sentences.en: But the actual thing that you need is a health care system that provides free kidney transplants to everyone.
sentences.zh: 但你真正需要的是一个能为所有人提供免费肾脏移植的医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: Like, that would be far more heartwarming.
sentences.zh: 比如，那才会让人感到无比温馨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I'll confess that I kind of felt the same way, which is actually what brings us to the other city I wanted to talk about, a place where things played out very differently.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我得承认我也有同感，这其实也就是我们要谈到另一个城市的原因，那里的情况走向了截然不同的方向。

sentences.en: Because while Detroit was struggling with just getting people online, this other city was busy getting crisscrossed with fiber connections.
sentences.zh: 因为当底特律还在为让人们联网而苦苦挣扎时，另一个城市正忙着铺设纵横交错的光纤连接。

sentences.en: And they did it by rethinking their entire approach to internet access.
sentences.zh: 他们通过重新思考整个互联网接入的方法做到了这一点。

sentences.en: We'll find out just what City Katie is talking about right after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将揭晓凯蒂所说的到底是哪座城市。

sentences.en: Support for this four-part series exploring the future of health and well-being comes from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation,
sentences.zh: 本期关于探索健康与福祉未来的四集系列节目得到了罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会的赞助支持，

sentences.en: which is committed to improving health and health equity in the United States.
sentences.zh: 该基金会致力于改善美国的健康状况和健康公平。

sentences.en: Knowing that the healthy, equitable future we all deserve won't simply arrive, RWJF is exploring how new technologies, scientific discoveries, cultural shifts,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·伍德·约翰逊基金会深知我们所有人应得的健康、公平的未来不会凭空降临，因此正在探索新技术、科学发现、文化变革，

sentences.en: and unforeseen events like those in today's story may shape our lives in years to come.
sentences.zh: 以及如今天故事中那些意想不到的事件将如何在未来几年塑造我们的生活。

sentences.en: Through these explorations, they're learning what it will take to build a future that provides every individual with a fair and just opportunity to thrive, no matter who they are,
sentences.zh: 通过这些探索，他们正在了解要打造一个怎样的未来才能为每个人提供公平公正的发展机会，无论他是谁，

sentences.en: where they live, or how much money they have.
sentences.zh: 住在哪里，或者有多少财富。

sentences.en: Learn more about their efforts at rwjf.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问rwjf.org了解更多关于他们工作的信息。

sentences.en: If you like thinking about the future of things as we've been doing in this series, and you have a hunch about what it will take to build an equitable future,
sentences.zh: 如果你和我们一样喜欢思考事物的未来，并且对建立一个公平的未来需要什么有直觉上的预感，

sentences.en: share it at shareyourhunch.org.
sentences.zh: 请在shareyourhunch.org上分享出来。

sentences.en: I'm submitting my hunch, so I'm going to shareyourhunch.org and selecting the prompt, I'm noticing that.
sentences.zh: 我正在提交我的预感，所以我去了shareyourhunch.org并选择了提示：我注意到。

sentences.en: I'm noticing that more people in their 40s and 50s are having a midlife crisis in terms of their careers and thinking earnestly about career changes that do not prioritize income.
sentences.zh: 我注意到越来越多40多岁和50多岁的人在职业生涯中遭遇了中年危机，并开始认真思考那些不把收入放在首位的职业转变。

sentences.en: That's my hunch.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的直觉预感。

sentences.en: Those are from conversations I have with other parents.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我与其他家长交谈时了解到的。

sentences.en: Check out other hunches and submit your own at shareyourhunch.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问shareyourhunch.org查看其他人的预感并提交你自己的看法。

sentences.en: We're back talking internet access with reporter Katie Thornton.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，我们继续与记者凯蒂·桑顿一起讨论互联网接入问题。

sentences.en: So, Katie, before the break, you were saying that there was another city you wanted to talk about where people had an easier time getting high-quality broadband.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯蒂，在休息之前，你提到过另一个城市，你想聊聊那里的人们是如何更轻松地获得高质量宽带的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没受。

sentences.en: And this is a place that, even during the very worst of COVID, more or less managed to avoid all of the connectivity problems we described earlier.
sentences.zh: 这个地方即使在新冠疫情最严重的时候，也多多少少避开了我们之前描述的所有连接问题。

sentences.en: In fact, in this one city, pretty much anyone who wanted to get good internet access during the pandemic could get it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在这个城市里，几乎任何在疫情期间想要获得良好互联网接入的人都能如愿以偿。

sentences.en: And contrary to what you might expect, it's not Westchester County or Grosse Pointe or Newport Beach or any of these uber-wealthy suburbs.
sentences.zh: 而且与你可能预期的相反，它不是韦斯特切斯特县、格罗斯波因特、纽波特比奇或任何这些超级富裕的郊区。

sentences.en: It's Chattanooga, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 而是田纳西州的查塔努加。

sentences.en: Practically overnight, our schools shut down.
sentences.zh: 几乎在一夜之间，我们的学校关闭了。

sentences.en: Many of our businesses moved to remote work.
sentences.zh: 我们的许多企业转为远程办公。

sentences.en: And being able to go home and immediately access services really enabled you to work at home, learn at home, without missing a beat.
sentences.zh: 能够回家并立即访问各种服务，真的让你能够在家里工作、在家里学习，而不会错过任何节奏。

sentences.en: So, who is this, and why does she have so much good news about Chattanooga?
sentences.zh: 那么，这位是谁？为什么她有这么多关于查塔努加的好消息？

sentences.en: So, this is Katie Esposeth.
sentences.zh: 这位是凯蒂·埃斯波塞斯。

sentences.en: She works at EPB, which is Chattanooga's city-run electric power utility.
sentences.zh: 她在查塔努加市营电力公司EPB工作。

sentences.en: And the reason she has such good news is because Chattanooga's great.
sentences.zh: 她之所以有这么好的消息，是因为查塔努加真的很棒。

sentences.en: But also because back in the mid-2000s, Chattanooga was kind of like Detroit.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为在21世纪头十年中期，查塔努加有点像底特律。

sentences.en: Internet access options for most telecom customers were really limited.
sentences.zh: 大多数电信客户的互联网接入选项非常有限。

sentences.en: Chattanooga was in very much an underserved area.
sentences.zh: 查塔努加在很大程度上属于服务匮乏地区。

sentences.en: While we did have service from two large national incumbents, really there was no competition.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们确实有来自两家大型全国性老牌运营商的服务，但实际上根本没有竞争。

sentences.en: And so, there was no real driver to provide better services.
sentences.zh: 因此，也没有提供更好服务的真正的动力。

sentences.en: But I do think we fell into a range of a lot of cities our size and that we were not getting the best technology.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们陷入了许多同规模城市常有的困境，那就是我们没有获得最好的技术。

sentences.en: So, they were kind of just in this motivational trough where these big providers had no incentive to provide anything beyond the slowest connection.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当时正处于这样一种动力低谷，这些大运营商没有任何动力去提供比最慢连接更好的服务。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But then, and this is the good news part, the city made a really interesting move.
sentences.zh: 但随后——这就是好消息所在——这座城市采取了一个非常有趣的举措。

sentences.en: They decided that starting in 2008, EPB, that public power utility that Katie works for, should enter the telecom market and become an internet provider.
sentences.zh: 他们决定从2008年开始，凯蒂工作的那个公共电力公司EPB应该进入电信市场，成为一家互联网供应商。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: So, EPB would compete with the existing providers to sell internet connections to businesses and households.
sentences.zh: 因此，EPB将与现有供应商竞争，向企业和家庭出售互联网连接。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: They already sold electricity to customers, and that's also not free.
sentences.zh: 他们已经向客户出售电力了，而且电力也不是免费的。

sentences.en: So, why not sell internet access too?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么不顺便也出售互联网接入服务呢？

sentences.en: And where we landed was using a fiber optic network.
sentences.zh: 我们最终采取的方案是使用光纤网络。

sentences.en: EPB already had power lines that reached every home and business in town, meaning they could put these super fast internet lines right alongside them.
sentences.zh: EPB已经拥有能够连接镇上每个家庭和企业的电力线，这意味着他们可以在这些电力线旁边直接铺设超高速互联网线路。

sentences.en: And so, EPB started laying down fiber all over the city.
sentences.zh: 于是EPB开始在全市范围内铺设光纤。

sentences.en: And they could afford to do fiber.
sentences.zh: 他们负担得起铺设光纤的费用吗？

sentences.en: Well, actually, yeah, they could, provided they got enough customers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，是的，只要他们能争取到足够的客户。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, as we were working through the business plan, we realized we needed about one in every three homes to make this profitable.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在我们制定商业计划的过程中，我们意识到大约需要三分之一的家庭使用才能实现盈利。

sentences.en: So, did you beat that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们突破这个目标了吗？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.en: We did beat that, no doubt.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对突破了。

sentences.en: We secured a greater than a 33 or a 30% take rate from the first month we were in business.
sentences.zh: 我们从营业的第一个月起就获得了超过33%（或30%）的采用率。

sentences.en: And so, how did those, you know, existing ISPs respond to that?
sentences.zh: 那么，那些已有的互联网服务供应商是如何回应的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it turned into a classic speed war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这演变成了一场经典的提速大战。

sentences.en: First, EPB offered a connection that was 30 megabits per second download speed and upload speed, which was a lot back then.
sentences.zh: 首先，EPB提供的连接下载和上传速度都是每秒30兆比特，这在当时已经很高了。

sentences.en: But their competitors weren't going to let that phase them.
sentences.zh: 但他们的竞争对手可不会让这影响到自己。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, they were not ready to give up market share without a fight.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，他们可不打算不经过一番较量就拱手让出市场份额。

sentences.en: So, when we launched with a 30 meg product, our competitor came back and they upgraded theirs to a 30 meg product.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们推出30兆的产品时，我们的竞争对手立刻回击，将他们的产品升级到了30兆。

sentences.en: So, then EPB upgraded to 50 megs.
sentences.zh: 于是EPB随后升级到了50兆。

sentences.en: And when their competitor matched that, they went to 100 and then 300.
sentences.zh: 当他们的竞争对手跟进时，他们又升级到了100兆，然后是300兆。

sentences.en: And in 2010, EPB began offering gigabit services, which was way ahead of the rest of the country at the time.
sentences.zh: 在2010年，EPB开始提供千兆服务，这在当时远远领先于全国其他地区。

sentences.en: In fact, when we rolled out a gig, we got so many questions over what would anyone do with a gig?
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我们推出千兆服务时，我们收到了很多质疑：到底谁会需要千兆？

sentences.en: This is just crazy.
sentences.zh: 这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: This is just marketing.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是营销噱头。

sentences.en: But after a while, those gig connections turned out to be really useful for things like streaming high-definition movies or uploading multimedia homework assignments.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，事实证明千兆连接对于流式传输高清电影或上传多媒体家庭作业等事情非常有用。

sentences.en: Or like zooming into every meeting during a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 或者像在疫情期间缩放到每个会议里。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think people have figured out what to do.
sentences.zh: 我想人们已经弄清楚该怎么用了。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any argument about what you do with a gig.
sentences.zh: 对于拿到千兆能干什么，现在应该没有任何争议了。

sentences.en: And so, in time, their competitors started offering gig speed services, too.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着时间的推移，他们的竞争对手也开始提供千兆速度的服务。

sentences.en: And, Roman, for EPB, this was a goal of theirs all along.
sentences.zh: 而且，罗曼，对EPB来说，这其实一直是他们的目标。

sentences.en: The idea was that even if EPB didn't dominate the market, they would foster competition and force the private companies to provide better services.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，即使EPB没有垄断市场，他们也能促进竞争，迫使私营公司提供更好的服务。

sentences.en: And that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: That is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: But also, like, did they ever dominate the market?
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，他们有没有统治过市场？

sentences.en: Did they ever make it to number one?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有做到过第一？

sentences.en: Eventually, yeah, they did.
sentences.zh: 最终，是的，他们做到了。

sentences.en: In 2017, we hit a mark of 75,000 customers.
sentences.zh: 在2017年，我们达到了75,000名客户的里程碑。

sentences.en: 2018, it was 100,000 customers.
Today, it's a little over 110,000 customers.
sentences.zh: 如今，客户数量略多于110,000名。

sentences.en: And so, do you have a sense of what your market share is right now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们现在对自己的市场份额大概有什么概念吗？

sentences.en: We sit at about 68% market share today.
sentences.zh: 我们目前的市场份额大约在68%左右。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, those ISPs were right to be afraid.
sentences.zh: 所以那些互联网服务供应商害怕得有理。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think that what's amazing about EPB is that the other third of people in their footprint who aren't using EPB,
sentences.zh: 我认为EPB最了不起的地方在于，他们服务范围内另外三分之一没有使用EPB的人，

sentences.en: they've already built out the fiber connections in front of those homes and businesses.
sentences.zh: EPB其实已经在这些家庭和企业门前铺设好了光纤连接。

sentences.en: So, all you need to do is sign up, and EPB will basically wire you up, hand you a modem, and poof, you are online.
sentences.zh: 所以你所需要做的只是注册登记，EPB基本上就会为你接通线路、交给你一个调制解调器，然后，咻，你就联网了。

sentences.en: Which kind of led me to what I thought might be a gotcha question, but it turned out to just be more good news.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到一个我以为可能会是个陷阱的问题，但结果证明它只是更多的好消息。

sentences.en: Did the uptake of the service vary depending on household income or depending on the race?
sentences.zh: 这项服务的采用率会根据家庭收入或种族的不同而有所差异吗？

sentences.en: You know, interestingly enough, no.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有趣的是，并没有。

sentences.en: Our take rate is pretty standard across all income brackets as well as different geographic areas within our footprint.
sentences.zh: 在所有收入阶层以及我们服务范围内的不同地理区域，我们的采用率都相当标准。

sentences.en: And part of that is because EPB has long provided an at-cost internet service for low-income families.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于EPB长期以来一直为低收入家庭提供按成本价计算的互联网服务。

sentences.en: And in the pandemic, they made it free.
sentences.zh: 而在疫情期间，他们将其变为了免费。

sentences.en: And all of this has had really real benefits.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都带来了非常真实的效益。

sentences.en: Economists predicted that citywide fiber would add 2,000 jobs over 10 years.
sentences.zh: 经济学家曾预测全市范围的光纤网络将在10年内增加2,000个工作岗位。

sentences.en: But according to some studies, it's actually added about 10,000 jobs.
sentences.zh: 但根据一些研究，它实际上已经增加了大约10,000个工作岗位。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And not long into the pandemic, the surrounding county's unemployment rate was 2% lower than the national average.
sentences.zh: 而且在大流行开始后不久，周边县的失业率比全国平均水平低了2%。

sentences.en: You know, it's really interesting because to hear you talk about how EPB rolled out their fiber network and the benefits of it,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的很有趣，因为听你谈论EPB如何推广他们的光纤网络以及它的好处时，

sentences.en: I almost have to remind myself that you're not talking about electricity because, like, it's really reminiscent of the way New Deal programs like the Tennessee Valley Authority
sentences.zh: 我几乎得提醒自己，你谈论的不是电力，因为这真的很让人想起诸如田纳西流域管理局之类的“新政”项目，

sentences.en: transformed electricity from a private commodity into a regulated utility to a point where it would just seem wrong that someone couldn't afford electricity.
sentences.zh: 它们把电力从一种私人商品转变为一种受管制的公用事业，甚至到了让人觉得有人用不起电才是不正常的程度。

sentences.en: And now EPB is doing the same thing but for internet access.
sentences.zh: 现在EPB正在做同样的事情，只不过对象换成了互联网接入。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's spot on.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，完全说到了点子上。

sentences.en: And that's not just your read of it.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是你个人的理解。

sentences.en: In our interview, Katie directly connected EPB's mission here to the TVA, which served Chattanooga.
sentences.zh: 在我们的采访中，凯蒂直接将EPB在这里的使命与服务查塔努加的田纳西流域管理局联系了起来。

sentences.en: You know, in the 1930s and really throughout the remainder of that century, the way to fulfill that mission was very obvious.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在20世纪30年代，以及实际上在该世纪的其余时间里，实现这一使命的方法是非常明确的。

sentences.en: It was all about bringing electrification to the valley.
sentences.zh: 那就是为整个流域带来电气化。

sentences.en: It meant jobs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着就业。

sentences.en: It meant industry.
sentences.zh: 这意味着工业。

sentences.en: It really meant survival.
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着生存。

sentences.en: And actually, we think today that high-speed internet or access to broadband services does the very same thing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们今天认为高速互联网或宽带服务的接入也起到了完全相同的作用。

sentences.en: I find this all super inspiring.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这一切都超级鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: And this seems like the top-down solution that really is necessary.
sentences.zh: 而且这似乎正是那种真正必不可少的自上而下的解决方案。

sentences.en: You know, like, this is sort of like, we're from the government.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就有点像是，我们来自政府。

sentences.en: We're here to help.
sentences.zh: 我们是来帮忙的。

sentences.en: And they really did help.
sentences.zh: 而他们确实帮了忙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我也有同感。

sentences.en: So this might be a naive question, but, like, if it works for Chattanooga, why can't it work for Detroit?
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是一个天真的问题，但是，如果它在查塔努加行得通，为什么在底特律就行不通呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, or everywhere?
sentences.zh: 对，或者说为什么不能在任何地方都行得通？

sentences.en: Like, exactly.
sentences.zh: 就是说，完全如此。

sentences.en: I want it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我希望到处都有。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely not a naive question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对不是一个天真的问题。

sentences.en: I wondered that, too.
sentences.zh: 我也一直在想这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, surely Chattanooga is proof that all you need to get Americans online is the political will.
sentences.zh: 比如，查塔努加无疑证明了让美国人上网所需要的全部条件就是政治意愿。

sentences.en: And this was 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且这已经是10年前的事了。

sentences.en: So why aren't we seeing a ton more of it?
sentences.zh: 那为什么我们没有看到更多这样的情况发生呢？

sentences.en: So why haven't we?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么我们还没有？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out it's not that easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明事情并没有那么简单。

sentences.en: There are some things that make Chattanooga a little bit of a unicorn.
sentences.zh: 有些因素让查塔努加显得有些独一无二。

sentences.en: And one of the big ones is that, remember, Chattanooga already has its own municipal electric system.
sentences.zh: 其中一个重大因素是，记住，查塔努加已经拥有自己的市政电力系统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that meant that when EPB wanted to run fiber lines,
sentences.zh: 这意味着当EPB想要铺设光纤线路时，

sentences.en: they could just do it by laying fiber right alongside their existing electric infrastructure that already went into people's homes.
sentences.zh: 他们只需顺着已经通进居民家中的现有电力基础设施直接铺设光纤即可。

sentences.en: And then that electricity actually powers the fiber, so they don't need to worry about that part either.
sentences.zh: 而且电力实际上还能为光纤供电，所以他们甚至不需要担心那部分问题。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，真有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And most cities just don't have an existing department that's in a position to do that.
sentences.zh: 大多数城市根本没有现成的部门能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: And if you're a mayor and you want to set one up, it's going to cost you a ton of money up front.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个市长，并且想建立这样一个部门，前期将花费你巨额资金。

sentences.en: And there's no way you're going to see tangible results before your next election.
sentences.zh: 而且你绝对不可能在下次选举前看到切实的结果。

sentences.en: So it's often a political non-starter.
sentences.zh: 所以这通常是一个在政治上无法启动的项目。

sentences.en: But it just seems like the size and cost of these infrastructure buildouts could be overcome if people really wanted to have a public internet.
sentences.zh: 但似乎只要人们真的想要公共互联网，这些基础设施建设的规模和成本是可以克服的。

sentences.en: Like, it would be expensive, but it would be possible.
sentences.zh: 比如，虽然会很昂贵，但这是可能的。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全同意。

sentences.en: Like, we should make that very clear.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们应该把这一点说清楚。

sentences.en: Like, these things are possible to overcome.
sentences.zh: 比如，这些困难是完全有可能克服的。

sentences.en: But, Roman, in many parts of the U.S., there's one thing that makes it more or less impossible.
sentences.zh: 但是，罗曼，在美国的许多地方，有一件事让这几乎变得不可能。

sentences.en: There are laws that exist today in the country in specific states that prohibit municipal broadband.
sentences.zh: 这个国家现在有些州的现行法律禁止市政宽带。

sentences.en: Of course there are.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: Of course they made it illegal.
sentences.zh: 当然他们会将其定为非法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道。

sentences.en: I wish that I was more surprised as well.
sentences.zh: 我也希望我能对此感到更惊讶一些。

sentences.en: But 18 states effectively have roadblocks that keep cities from offering internet.
sentences.zh: 但有18个州实际上设置了路障，阻止城市提供互联网服务。

sentences.en: And another five states have laws that make it really difficult.
sentences.zh: 另外还有五个州的法律让这件事变得极其艰难。

sentences.en: And those laws have been pushed by for-profit internet companies and their very powerful lobbying arms for years.
sentences.zh: 这些法律多年来一直受到营利性互联网公司及其极具权力的游说团体的推动。

sentences.en: And so what are their bullshit arguments against public broadband?
sentences.zh: 那么他们反对公共互联网的那些荒谬论调是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I reached out to folks at the two biggest telecom lobbies for this story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了这个故事，我联系了两大电信游说团体的相关人员。

sentences.en: They didn't agree to interviews.
sentences.zh: 他们没有接受采访。

sentences.en: But traditionally they've said municipal broadband interferes with free markets, that it's not the government's place, etc.
sentences.zh: 但传统上他们一直声称，市政宽带干扰了自由市场，这不是政府该管的事，等等。

sentences.en: But Greta says ISPs also argue, we've been doing this for decades, so we have the know-how.
sentences.zh: 但格雷塔说，ISP（互联网服务提供商）还辩称，我们已经做了几十年，所以我们拥有专业知识。

sentences.en: And so, you know, like if you're a local official and you have a big telecom company saying,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你是一个地方官员，有一家大电信公司对你说，

sentences.en: hey, we've got that, we're going to take care of it for you,
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们搞定了，我们会为你处理好的，

sentences.en: you know, that can sound kind of good to a local politician, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这听起来对地方政治家来说可能挺不错的，对吧？

sentences.en: Who's like, I don't understand how this stuff works.
sentences.zh: 他们会想，我又不懂这东西是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: Like, just fix it for me.
sentences.zh: 那就帮我修好得了。

sentences.en: And the result is that these lobbies have pretty successfully put the brakes on a lot of municipal broadband.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，这些游说团体相当成功地踩下了许多市政宽带的刹车。

sentences.en: And so in many states and cities and rural areas, private ISPs are the only ones allowed to provide these services.
sentences.zh: 因此，在许多州、城市和农村地区，私营ISP是唯一被允许提供这些服务的人。

sentences.en: And so is that true for Detroit?
sentences.zh: 那么底特律也是这样吗？

sentences.en: Like, does Michigan have these laws that prevent publicly owned ISPs?
sentences.zh: 密歇根州是否有这种阻止全民所有制ISP的法律？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: And although the situation in Detroit has improved somewhat in the last decade,
sentences.zh: 尽管底特律的情况在过去十年里有所改善，

sentences.en: even today, they're still ranked in the bottom 10 for American cities when it comes to Internet access.
sentences.zh: 但即使在今天，在互联网接入方面，他们仍然在全美城市中排在倒数前十位。

sentences.en: The private ISP model hasn't yielded big changes,
sentences.zh: 私营ISP模式并没有带来重大的改变，

sentences.en: all of which has left some people, like Patrick Crouch, feeling almost kind of resigned to their fates.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切让帕特里克·克劳奇这样的一些人对自己的命运感到几乎有些逆来顺受。

sentences.en: What did you do for Internet when you moved?
sentences.zh: 你搬家时是用什么上网的？

sentences.en: Get Comcast, like a normal human being.
sentences.zh: 办康卡斯特（Comcast），就像个正常人一样。

sentences.en: I mean, are you happy with your service?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你对你的服务满意吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不满意。

sentences.en: But, you know, it had just come to a point where we didn't really have a lot of options.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，事情已经到了这个地步，我们确实没有太多选择。

sentences.en: And as I mentioned, Comcast is really the only game in town.
sentences.zh: 正如我所提到的，康卡斯特真的是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: Man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So if this is where things are still now, if Mesh Network won't scale,
sentences.zh: 所以如果事情至今仍然如此，如果网状网络无法扩展，

sentences.en: if municipal-owned broadband is logistically and politically hard, where does that leave us?
sentences.zh: 如果市政拥有的宽带在后勤和政治上都很困难，那我们将何去何从？

sentences.en: Like, what can be done or is being done from here on out to get everyone good Internet that they need?
sentences.zh: 比如，从现在开始，可以做些什么或者正在做些什么，来让每个人都获得他们需要的优质互联网？

sentences.en: Well, the short answer is no one is totally sure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简而言之，没有人能完全确定。

sentences.en: The recent infrastructure bill looks like it's going to help with building out fiber in rural areas.
sentences.zh: 最近的基础设施法案看起来将有助于在农村地区铺设光纤。

sentences.en: And the people distributing a lot of the money to the states are asking explicitly about digital equity in cities.
sentences.zh: 而向各州分发大量资金的人正在明确询问城市中的数字公平问题。

sentences.en: But in those states with bans on municipal broadband, that money is most likely going to keep going to ISPs.
sentences.zh: 但在那些禁止市政宽带的州，这些资金很可能会继续流向ISP。

sentences.en: And if the past is any indication, those ISPs might just end up using it to offer further discounts on the same old, outdated Internet connection,
sentences.zh: 如果过去可以作为参考的话，这些ISP最终可能只会用这些资金对陈旧的旧互联网连接提供进一步的折扣，

sentences.en: rather than building anything new.
sentences.zh: 而不是建设任何新东西。

sentences.en: At least in neighborhoods like Detroit's North End.
sentences.zh: 至少在底特律北端这样的社区是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which is why, although Greta and Monique both think there's room for collaboration with ISPs,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么尽管格雷塔和莫妮卡都认为有与ISP合作的空间，

sentences.en: Monique stresses that any solution needs to lie in giving access to those who have long been on the margins of technology.
sentences.zh: 但莫妮卡强调，任何解决方案都需要在于向长期处于科技边缘的人们提供接入服务。

sentences.en: Where do I see things going from here?
sentences.zh: 我认为事情从这里会如何发展？

sentences.en: I do look at the provision of Internet as a potential opportunity to execute reparations.
sentences.zh: 我确实将互联网的提供视为执行赔偿的一个潜在机会。

sentences.en: Yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: Monique says that whatever happens in the long term, in the immediate future, it's time for big telecom companies to step up.
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡说，无论长远来看发生什么，在不久的将来，各大电信公司是时候加把劲了。

sentences.en: They can't just follow the money and only lay down fiber in the richest neighborhoods anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不能再只跟着金钱走，只在最富裕的社区铺设光纤了。

sentences.en: They have to build out.
sentences.zh: 他们必须进行扩展。

sentences.en: Big telecom has the largest profit margins in the country.
sentences.zh: 大型电信公司拥有全国最高的利润率。

sentences.en: So why not give back?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么不回馈社会呢？

sentences.en: CEOs say that they are giving to communities in need.
sentences.zh: 首席执行官们说他们正在回馈有需要的社区。

sentences.en: Well, give what we need.
sentences.zh: 好吧，给我们真正需要的东西。

sentences.en: Give Internet.
sentences.zh: 给我们互联网。

sentences.en: Just give us the access.
sentences.zh: 只要给我们接入权限。

sentences.en: And we'll go from there.
sentences.zh: 然后我们再从长计议。

sentences.en: So ultimately, it's going to be tricky.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，这将是棘手的。

sentences.en: The goal of for-profit companies will always be to make money.
sentences.zh: 营利性公司的目标永远是赚钱。

sentences.en: Which is why a lot of people still believe that quality Internet access for everyone means eventually treating broadband as a right, not just a commodity.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么许多人仍然认为，为每个人提供高质量的互联网接入意味着最终将宽带视为一项权利，而不仅仅是一项商品。

sentences.en: And that requires intervention by people who are accountable to votes and not just dollars.
sentences.zh: 这需要那些对选票负责而不仅仅是对美元负责的人进行干预。

sentences.en: But no matter what happens next, if we know one thing, it's that the days of treating broadband as a luxury are over.
sentences.zh: 但无论接下来发生什么，如果我们知道一件事，那就是将宽带视为奢侈品的时代已经结束了。
